definitions.gloss: to speak one's true feelings; to reveal one's real thoughts; to let one's true feelings slip out
definitions.explanation: To express what one truly thinks or feels, often after holding back. Implies that the true feelings were previously hidden behind a polite or official front (建前).

examples.japanese: ついに{本音|ほんね}を{吐|は}いた。
examples.english: He finally spoke his true feelings.

examples.japanese: ⟦お{酒|さけ}→お酒：01045_osake⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{飲|の}む→飲む：00322_nomu⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧{本音|ほんね}を{吐|は}きやすく⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: When you drink, it becomes easier to let your true feelings out.

examples.japanese: ⟦{会議|かいぎ}→会議：00710_kaigi⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{誰|だれ}も→誰も：18610_daremo⟧{本音|ほんね}を{吐|は}かなかった⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧、⟦{飲|の}み{会|かい}→飲み会：09371_nomikai⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{不満|ふまん}→不満：02497_fuman⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{出|で}た→出る：00513_deru⟧。
examples.english: No one spoke their true feelings at the meeting, but complaints came out at the drinking party.

notes:
USAGE:
The verb ⟦{吐|は}く→吐く：04397_haku⟧ here means "to let out" or "to utter" (not "to vomit"). This expression is closely tied to the Japanese cultural concept of ⟦{本音|ほんね}→本音：06620_honne⟧ (true feelings) versus ⟦{建前|たてまえ}→建前：06621_tatemae⟧ (public facade).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- つい{本音|ほんね}を{吐|は}く (to accidentally let one's true feelings slip)
- {本音|ほんね}を{吐|は}きやすい⟦{場|ば}→場：03699_ba⟧ (a setting where it's easy to be honest)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{本音|ほんね}→本音：06620_honne⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{言|い}う→言う：00515_iu⟧: to say what one really thinks — more neutral
- ⟦{本音|ほんね}→本音：06620_honne⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{漏|も}らす→漏らす：02436_morasu⟧: to let one's true feelings leak out — implies it was unintentional
- ⟦{腹|はら}→腹：02165_hara⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{割|わ}って→割る：02334_waru⟧⟦{話|はな}す→話す：00467_hanasu⟧: to speak frankly — emphasizes openness in conversation
